register.name: Azerbaijan Scaling-Up Renewable Energy Project (AZURE)
register.detail: World Bank · IBRD loan · P505208 · approved 27 March 2025
register.note: The World Bank says it will help unlock an initial $384 million of private investment
register.text: An IBRD loan approved on 27 March 2025 to connect the 240-megawatt Absheron-Garadagh Wind Power Plant to the transmission grid and to strengthen and expand the 330/500 kV grid to carry up to 1 GW of privately developed renewable power. It serves the energy standard with reliable, affordable and sustainable electricity for households and businesses.

register.name: Employment Support Project, additional financing
register.note: World Bank Group Finances One lists US$150,000,000 approved on 29 July 2024 (data as of 31 July 2026)
register.text: Additional financing of US$150 million for the World Bank’s Employment Support Project in Azerbaijan, approved on 29 July 2024. It serves the livelihood standard by scaling up employment support across the country.

register.name: Baku Metro Signaling Modernization and Operations Digitalization Project
register.detail: ADB loan · approved 13 October 2026 · AIIB cofinancing $79.98 million · total cost $515.07 million
register.note: Baku Metro carried about 220.4 million passenger boardings in 2025; the Government provides $132.71 million
register.text: An ADB loan to replace the Baku Metro signaling system with communications-based train control, upgrade its operations control centre and digital systems, and train its workforce, with measures to raise the share of women in technical and digital roles. Part of the Government of Azerbaijan’s $2.6 billion Baku Metro expansion programme, it serves the livelihood standard through safer and more reliable journeys to work in the capital.

register.name: Bilajari–Yalama railway modernization
register.detail: ADB loan · approved 6 October 2026 · 192-kilometre double-track line
register.note: Electrification, signaling and telecommunications on one of Azerbaijan’s most important international freight routes
register.text: An ADB loan to install modern electrification, signaling and telecommunication systems along the 192-kilometre double-track railway between Bilajari and Yalama, and to strengthen the project management capacity of Azerbaijan Railways. It serves the livelihood standard through trade and transport, and opens technical, supervisory and management roles to women.

register.name: Reconstruction of the Garabagh Irrigation Canal
register.detail: IsDB financing · signed 18 June 2026 at the IsDB Group Annual Meetings in Baku · about 168 km of canal
register.note: Aims to reduce water losses by approximately 30 percent
register.text: IsDB financing for the reconstruction and modernisation of around 168 kilometres of the Garabagh irrigation canal, with smart water management systems, signed on 18 June 2026. It serves the water and food standards: less water lost, more reliable delivery and more irrigated land for farming.

register.name: Shaki Water and Wastewater Project
register.detail: EBRD sovereign loan · project 56006 · Tranche 1 up to €57 million; Tranche 2 up to €34 million (uncommitted) · notice of 12 May 2026
register.note: Approval and signing are not stated in the notice; Tranche 1 is co-financed by an E5P investment grant of up to €4 million; the client is the Azerbaijan State Water Resources Agency
register.text: A sovereign loan of up to €91 million to the Republic of Azerbaijan to complete the Shaki wastewater treatment plant, with a capacity of 16,000 m³ a day, and to build water supply and sewerage networks, water reservoirs and stormwater drains. It serves the water standard, the furthest from reach in Azerbaijan, and the sanitation measure of the shelter standard.

register.name: Baku Metro Expansion Project, Phase I
register.detail: AIIB sovereign-backed loan · approved 6 February 2026 · borrower: Ministry of Finance
register.note: Two depots and upgrades at 10 existing Green Line stations
register.text: An AIIB loan to the Republic of Azerbaijan to build two depots, including the Darnagul depot, and to carry out safety, environmental, social and climate upgrades at 10 existing Green Line stations of the Baku Metro. It serves the livelihood standard through access to work across the capital.

register.name: Main Irrigation Canal from the Maiden Tower Reservoir
register.detail: IsDB · signed at COP29 in Baku, 2024 · $96.48 million of IsDB ordinary capital and $250,000 of Waqf funds
register.note: To supply water to 8,400 hectares of agricultural land in Jabrayil and Fuzuli
register.text: A main irrigation canal to supply water to 8,400 hectares of agricultural land in the districts of Jabrayil and Fuzuli, with a total cost of US$96.73 million financed by the IsDB, signed on the sidelines of COP29 in Baku in 2024. It serves the food and water standards.

register.name: Loan to Bank Respublika for women-led MSMEs and agriculture
register.detail: ADB loan · signed 26 October 2026 · at least 20% to women-owned MSMEs, at least 50% to agriculture
register.note: For micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in the regions outside Baku
register.text: An ADB loan to Bank Respublika, signed on 26 October 2026, for on-lending to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in the regions outside Baku. At least 20% goes to women-owned firms and at least 50% to borrowers in agricultural production, processing and trade, serving the livelihood and food standards.

register.name: Senior loan to AccessBank for MSMEs
register.detail: FMO · three-year multi-currency senior loan · announced 13 November 2025
register.note: A particular focus on women-led, youth-led and agricultural businesses
register.text: A three-year multi-currency senior loan from FMO, the Dutch entrepreneurial development bank, to AccessBank to support micro-entrepreneurs and small and medium-sized enterprises, with a particular focus on women-led, youth-led and agricultural businesses. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Loan to AccessBank for MSME lending, second tranche
register.detail: EBRD · second tranche of an expanded facility · announced 16 May 2025
register.note: Announced by AccessBank; the signing date is not stated
register.text: A second tranche of US$10 million from the EBRD to AccessBank to further support lending to micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in Azerbaijan. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Bilasuvar and Neftchala solar projects (760 MW)
register.detail: Masdar and SOCAR Green · financial close 17 November 2024 · 445 MWac Bilasuvar, 315 MWac Neftchala
register.note: Total cost expected to be more than US$600 million; loan amounts by lender not stated
register.text: Financing secured from the EBRD, the ADB and the AIIB for two solar plants developed by Masdar and SOCAR Green: 445 MWac at Bilasuvar and 315 MWac at Neftchala. They serve the energy standard by adding renewable power to the grid.

register.name: Loan to AccessBank for microloans and entrepreneurship
register.detail: responsAbility Investment AG · three-year loan through two financial inclusion funds · announced 15 December 2025
register.note: Microloan financing named as a key priority
register.text: A three-year loan from responsAbility, a Swiss impact investor, channelled through two financial inclusion funds it manages, to support entrepreneurship in Azerbaijan, with microloan financing as a key priority. It serves the livelihood standard.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 21.2% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: FINCA Azerbaijan
items.text: A microfinance institution licensed by the Central Bank since 1999 whose Hybrid Agricultural Insurance Loan covers half of farmers’ insurance premiums and provides an agricultural microloan; the Microfinance Centre and the Azerbaijan Micro-Finance Association recognised it at COP30. Rural residents make up 70% of its clients, and it has served nearly three-quarters of a million people in Azerbaijan.

items.name: Viator
items.text: A microcredit institution that began in 1999 as a project of the Norwegian Humanitarian Enterprise, with the mission of helping poor people increase their income through adapted and sustainable microfinance services. A partner of the Grameen Crédit Agricole Foundation since 2011.

items.name: Kashalata Café
items.text: The first inclusive café in Baku, initiated by the public association Birgə və Sağlam, employs 20 young people, some of them with autism spectrum disorder and other neurodiverse characteristics. It continues its operations with the support of PASHA Holding and other partners.
